label: EDPB Guidelines 2/2023 — Technical Scope of Art. 5(3) ePrivacy (EU only — no legal status in the UK)
body: • Art. 5(3) is technology-neutral. The four cumulative criteria: information; terminal equipment of subscriber/user; public communications network; gaining access OR storing information.

• Use cases caught by Art. 5(3) (consent required unless strictly necessary): URL/pixel tracking; tracking-only HTTP referer or fingerprinting via JS that reads device characteristics; local processing where the result is sent back to the server; intermittent and mediated IoT reporting; unique identifiers in headers (e.g. operator-injected unique header).
• IP-only tracking: even passive IP collection can engage Art. 5(3) where there is "instruction to terminal equipment" to send identifying data (e.g. CDN with persistent cookies).
• Local processing: even if no data leaves the device, if the processor instructs the terminal to perform a specific computation that wouldn't otherwise occur, Art. 5(3) may apply.
• Strictly-necessary exemption applies only to: (i) sole purpose of transmission, or (ii) strictly necessary for an information society service explicitly requested by the user — narrow.
